title: NCLEX-RN Examinations (CAT & Next-Gen NGN Mock Suite)
subtitle: Dedicated NCLEX-RN simulation course featuring timed 60–100 question examinations across all 8 NCSBN Client Needs categories with detailed Saunders & Kaplan rationales.

exams.title: Exam 1: NCLEX-RN Diagnostic Readiness Examination (75 Questions)
exams.description: Balanced diagnostic simulation across Safe & Effective Care, Health Promotion, Psychosocial & Physiological Integrity.

questions.prompt: Jane, a 45-year-old woman, comes to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain. She has a history of chronic pancreatitis. The nurse is planning care for Jane. Which of the following would be the most appropriate nursing intervention?
options: Encouraging Jane to drink plenty of fluids
Assisting Jane with deep breathing exercises
Ordering a low-fat diet for Jane
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administering pain medication as ordered (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is experiencing thyroid nodules. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease thyroid hormone production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Central vision loss (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 10-year-old child with ADHD has been prescribed methylphenidate (Ritalin). The nurse should instruct the parents to monitor the child for which of the following adverse effects?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decreased appetite (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 15-year-old child with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus is admitted to the hospital for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Which of the following would the nurse expect to observe?
questions.rationale: Kussmaul respirations (rapid, deep breathing) are a common symptom of DKA, as the body tries to compensate for metabolic acidosis by blowing off excess carbon dioxide. Hypoglycemia (option A) is not typically associated with DKA; instead, blood glucose levels are usually high. Bradycardia (option B) and decreased urine output (option D) are not typical symptoms of DKA.

questions.prompt: The parents of a 2-year-old child with short bowel syndrome are concerned about their child's nutrition. Which of the following is an appropriate recommendation by the nurse?
options: The child should consume a high-fiber diet.
The child may require parenteral nutrition.
The child should avoid all fats in the diet.
The child should consume more dairy products.
questions.rationale: Short bowel syndrome can lead to malabsorption of nutrients. In severe cases, parenteral nutrition may be required to ensure the child receives adequate nutrition. A high-fiber diet (option A) may not be appropriate as it can increase stool output. Avoiding all fats (option C) is not recommended as some fat is necessary for growth and development. While some children with short bowel syndrome may tolerate dairy products (option D), others may not due to lactose intolerance.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. The nurse notes decreased breath sounds in the lower lobes of both lungs. What should the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Decreased breath sounds in the bases of the lungs indicate mucus accumulation, which can be mobilized with chest physiotherapy.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing dietary education to the parents of a child with celiac disease. Which food should the nurse instruct the parents to eliminate from the child's diet?
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is a disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Gluten is found in wheat, rye, and barley. Therefore, wheat should be eliminated from the diet of a child with celiac disease. Rice (option A), corn (option C), and potatoes (option D) are naturally gluten-free and can be included in the diet.

questions.prompt: A patient with Cushing's syndrome is experiencing weight gain and hypertension. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease cortisol production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The RN is delegating tasks to a licensed practical nurse (LPN). Which of the following tasks is appropriate for the RN to delegate to the LPN?
options: Monitoring a patient's response to medications
questions.rationale: Correct option: Monitoring a patient's response to medications (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient is diagnosed with cardiomyopathy. Which of the following signs and symptoms should the nurse expect to observe?
options: Swelling in the legs and feet
Weight loss and decreased urine output
questions.rationale: Correct option: Fatigue and shortness of breath (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with Addison's disease is experiencing adrenal insufficiency. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer hydrocortisone (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of hypoglycemia. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer glucose (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient presents with a sudden onset of dyspnea. The nurse auscultates the lung and hears a high-pitched sound on inspiration. What could this indicate?
questions.rationale: Stridor is a high-pitched, inspiratory sound that is often heard in acute laryngeal obstruction. It is a medical emergency and requires immediate attention.

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old child with asthma has been prescribed a metered-dose inhaler (MDI). The child is having difficulty coordinating inhalation with medication release. What is the best recommendation the nurse can make?
options: Try using a different type of inhaler.
Use a spacer with the MDI.
Practice more until the child gets it right.
Have a parent administer the medication.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Use a spacer with the MDI. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A client is prescribed a bronchodilator and a corticosteroid inhaler for treatment of asthma. Which of the following should the nurse instruct the client to do?
options: Use both inhalers at the same time
It does not matter which inhaler is used first
questions.rationale: The bronchodilator should be used first to open up the airways, allowing the corticosteroid inhaler to be more effective.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient who may have a perforated eardrum. Which of the following symptoms would likely be present?
questions.rationale: A perforated eardrum can cause ringing in the ears (tinnitus), sudden cessation of ear pain (as the pressure is relieved by the perforation), and hearing loss. Therefore, all of these symptoms might be present if a patient has a perforated eardrum.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with tuberculosis. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to prevent the spread of the disease?
options: Wear a mask when providing direct patient care
Place the patient in a private room
questions.rationale: Tuberculosis is an airborne disease. It is crucial to wear a mask, place the patient in a private room, and wash hands after removing gloves to prevent the spread of the disease.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who reports a sudden loss of hearing in one ear. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
options: Schedule the patient for a hearing test
Report the symptom to the healthcare provider
questions.rationale: Correct option: Report the symptom to the healthcare provider (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 10-year-old child with a brain tumor is scared about an upcoming surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate nursing action?
options: Reassure the child that everything will be okay
Explain the procedure in medical terms
Use simple, age-appropriate language to explain the procedure
Tell the child not to worry because the doctors are very good
questions.rationale: The best approach when communicating with a child is to use simple, age-appropriate language to explain procedures. This can help alleviate fears and anxiety. Options A and D may minimize the child's feelings, while option B may be too complex for a 10-year-old to understand.

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted with a pulmonary embolism. Which of the following is the priority nursing intervention?
questions.rationale: The immediate priority for a patient with a pulmonary embolism is to improve oxygenation, which can be achieved by providing supplemental oxygen.

questions.prompt: Question: A nurse is teaching a group of parents about growth hormone deficiency in children. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: It results in accelerated growth and development.
It is usually diagnosed during adolescence.
It can lead to short stature if left untreated.
questions.rationale: Correct option: It results in accelerated growth and development. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A parent brings her child to the clinic, concerned about small, skin-colored, dome-shaped bumps on the child's hands. The nurse recognizes these as a common childhood skin infection caused by a virus. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Molluscum contagiosum (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 2-year-old child admitted with bronchiolitis. Which of the following nursing interventions is most appropriate for this child?
options: Start the child on a high-fiber diet
questions.rationale: Correct option: Encourage fluid intake (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been prescribed a liquid medication. The prescription calls for 5 mL to be given twice daily. The parents are unsure how to measure this amount. What should the nurse recommend?
options: Use a teaspoon from the kitchen.
Use the dropper that came with the medication.
Use a syringe without a needle.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Use a syringe without a needle. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Diabetic neuropathy (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis is started on a regimen of multiple antibiotics. What should the nurse include in patient teaching regarding this treatment?
options: The patient will need to be on antibiotics for several weeks
The patient should expect a rapid improvement in symptoms
The patient should not drink alcohol while on these medications
questions.rationale: Tuberculosis requires a prolonged treatment with multiple antibiotics, often for several months. The patient should be cautioned not to drink alcohol while on these medications due to potential for liver damage. It's also important to inform the patient that although they might feel better, they need to finish the full course of antibiotics to fully treat the infection.

questions.prompt: A patient with cystic fibrosis has thick, tenacious secretions. Which medication would the nurse expect to administer to help the patient clear these secretions?
questions.rationale: Mucolytic medications help to thin and loosen mucus in the airways, making it easier to cough up. This can be helpful for patients with cystic fibrosis, who often have thick, sticky mucus in their lungs.

questions.prompt: Mr. Johnson, a 70-year-old man, has been diagnosed with congestive heart failure. He is experiencing shortness of breath and has gained 5 pounds in the last week. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention for Mr. Johnson?
options: Encouraging him to restrict his fluid intake
Assisting him with ambulation to increase his activity level
Administering a diuretic as ordered by the physician
Encouraging him to increase his sodium intake
questions.rationale: Correct option: Encouraging him to restrict his fluid intake (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with type 2 diabetes is taking metformin. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Increase insulin production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 2-month-old infant is brought to the clinic for a well-baby check-up. Which of the following developmental milestones would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Rolling over from back to stomach
Smiling in response to familiar faces
questions.rationale: Correct option: Smiling in response to familiar faces (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient on mechanical ventilation. The low-pressure alarm sounds. What is the most likely cause?
options: The patient is coughing or has a bronchospasm
The ventilator tubing has become disconnected
The patient is biting on the endotracheal tube
questions.rationale: A low-pressure alarm indicates a decrease in airway pressure, which may be caused by a disconnection or leak in the ventilator tubing.

questions.prompt: A 1-year-old child weighing 10 kg is ordered amoxicillin at a dose of 25 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. How many milligrams of amoxicillin will the nurse administer for each dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 125 mg (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a diagnosis of emphysema. Which of the following clinical manifestations would be expected?
questions.rationale: Emphysema is characterized by prolonged expiration due to loss of elastic recoil and air trapping in the lungs.

questions.prompt: The nurse is preparing to administer a vaccine to a 2-month-old infant. Which site is the most appropriate for this injection?
questions.rationale: Correct option: The vastus lateralis muscle (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with chronic bronchitis has poor appetite and has lost weight. What dietary modification should the nurse suggest?
questions.rationale: Patients with chronic bronchitis often have difficulty eating and may lose weight. A high-protein, high-calorie diet can help to maintain their nutritional status and support their immune function.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a diagnosis of emphysema. The nurse would expect to find which of the following during the physical assessment?
questions.rationale: Emphysema is characterized by an increased anterior-posterior diameter (often referred to as "barrel chest") due to hyperinflation of the alveoli.

questions.prompt: A patient on a ventilator is experiencing a decrease in oxygen saturation. The nurse increases the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) but the saturation does not improve. What should the nurse do next?
options: Increase the respiratory rate on the ventilator
questions.rationale: The nurse should next perform endotracheal suctioning to clear any secretions that might be obstructing the airway and affecting oxygenation. If this does not improve oxygenation, other interventions such as increasing PEEP may be considered.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma is prescribed a short-acting beta2-agonist and a glucocorticoid inhaler. Which medication should the nurse instruct the patient to use first?
options: Neither, they should be used simultaneously
questions.rationale: The short-acting beta2-agonist should be used first to dilate the bronchioles and improve airflow. This will then enhance the distribution and absorption of the glucocorticoid inhaler.

questions.prompt: A patient with heart failure presents with confusion and anxiety. What is the primary cause of these symptoms?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Fluid overload (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is scheduled for a corneal transplant. Which of the following is a key preoperative responsibility of the nurse?
options: Ensuring the patient has a clear understanding of the procedure
Verifying that the patient has arranged for help at home after discharge
questions.rationale: All of these actions are important nursing responsibilities before a corneal transplant. The patient should understand the procedure, any risks, and postoperative care, have preoperative antibiotics to prevent infection, and ensure they have arranged for help at home postoperatively as vision may be impaired.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with a suspected diagnosis of Meniere's disease. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to find?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Tinnitus (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is experiencing tachycardia and tremors. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer beta blockers (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of stroke is experiencing difficulty swallowing. Which of the following sensory disturbances is the patient most likely experiencing?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Dysphagia (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is experiencing thyroid storm. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer beta blockers (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with Cushing's syndrome is taking ketoconazole. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease cortisol production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with HIV/AIDS presents with a CD4 cell count of 200 cells/mm³. What opportunistic infection would the nurse be most concerned about?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 10-year-old child is undergoing radiation therapy for a brain tumour. Which of the following side effects is the child most likely to experience?
questions.rationale: While radiation therapy can potentially cause all these side effects, hair loss is the most common and immediate side effect of radiation therapy to the brain.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 6-month-old infant with Down syndrome. Which of the following interventions should be included in the nursing care plan?
options: Limit physical activity to prevent overexertion
Restrict social interaction to prevent overstimulation
Avoid discussing the diagnosis with the family
questions.rationale: Correct option: Encourage regular, age-appropriate developmental stimulation (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hypoparathyroidism is experiencing muscle cramps and tetany. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer calcium supplements (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperparathyroidism is experiencing bone pain. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease calcium levels (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with type 1 diabetes is experiencing diabetic retinopathy. What is the nurse's primary goal?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Improve vision (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The patient reports increased shortness of breath and a productive cough. What should be the nurse's primary action?
options: Increase the patient's oxygen flow rate
questions.rationale: Before initiating treatment, the nurse should first perform a thorough respiratory assessment to gather data about the patient's current condition. This will help guide further interventions and treatments.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?
options: Communicate the rationale for the change.
Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.
questions.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. Explaining the rationale for the change (B) helps staff understand the importance and necessity of the change, thereby fostering compliance. Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching safety precautions to a client with a hearing impairment. Which of the following should be included in the teaching plan?
options: Install smoke detectors with strobe lights
questions.rationale: Correct option: Install smoke detectors with strobe lights (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperparathyroidism is taking calcitonin. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease calcium levels (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: Medical records reveal that this client has a history of schizophrenia. Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate from the primary healthcare provider (PHCP) based on the history and physical?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Levodopa-Carbidopa← Parkinson?!?! (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of gastroparesis. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer metoclopramide (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The nurse is providing discharge teaching for the parents of an infant with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Which instruction should be included?
options: Feed the infant larger, less frequent meals
Position the infant flat after feeding
Thicken the infant's formula with rice cereal
Change the formula to a cow's milk-based formula
questions.rationale: Correct option: Thicken the infant's formula with rice cereal (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient reports vertigo and tinnitus. This patient is most likely experiencing which of the following conditions?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Meniere's disease (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you observe a conflict between two team members. What is the most appropriate initial action?
options: Ignore the conflict and hope it resolves itself.
Immediately report the incident to higher management.
Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue.
Take sides with the person who has been with the team longer.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following interventions would be most beneficial for this patient?
questions.rationale: Increased fluid intake can help thin out thick secretions in the lungs, making them easier to cough up and improving oxygenation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following symptoms should the nurse expect to find in a client diagnosed with right-sided heart failure?
questions.rationale: Right-sided heart failure results in systemic congestion, which manifests as peripheral edema. Crackles in the lungs, productive cough, and orthopnea are associated with left-sided heart failure due to pulmonary congestion.

questions.prompt: What type of heart failure does this statement describe? The ventricle is unable to properly fill with blood because it is too stiff. Therefore, blood backs up into the lungs causing the patient to experience shortness of breath.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A. True or false - should I withhold the client’s scheduled dose?
options: True or false - should I administer the dose as prescribed?
True or false - should I assess the client's urinary output?
True or false - should I assess the client's most recent sodium level?
True or false - should I assess the client’s heart rate and rhythm?
questions.rationale: Correct option: True or false - should I administer the dose as prescribed? (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been admitted to the hospital. Which of the following findings would the nurse expect to observe during the assessment?
questions.rationale: Patients with COPD often have difficulty exhaling, leading to a prolonged expiratory phase. The other options are not typical findings in COPD.

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer insulin (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 3-year-old child with gastroenteritis. Which of the following signs would indicate dehydration?
questions.rationale: Dehydration in children with gastroenteritis is a common complication due to fluid loss from vomiting and diarrhea. Decreased urinary output is a sign of dehydration. Increased blood pressure (option A) and decreased heart rate (option B) are not typical signs of dehydration. A sunken fontanelle (option C) could indicate dehydration, but it is not applicable in this case as the fontanelles are typically closed by age 2.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is scheduled for a cataract surgery. What is the most important preoperative nursing responsibility?
options: Teaching the patient about the surgery
Ensuring the patient is NPO after midnight
Ensuring informed consent has been obtained
questions.rationale: While all of these nursing responsibilities are important, ensuring that informed consent has been obtained is crucial. The patient must fully understand the procedure, the risks, benefits, and alternatives, and voluntarily agree to the surgery.

questions.prompt: You are the charge nurse on a paediatric oncology unit. Which patient should you assess first?
options: A child with leukemia and a fever of 101.5°F
A child with bone cancer complaining of pain
A child who is crying following the insertion of a central line
A child who is refusing to eat after chemotherapy
questions.rationale: Correct option: A child with leukemia and a fever of 101.5°F (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a child with Hirschsprung disease. Which of the following symptoms is most common in this condition?
questions.rationale: Hirschsprung disease is a congenital condition characterized by the absence of nerve cells in part of the intestine, resulting in chronic constipation. Diarrhea (option A), vomiting (option C), and abdominal pain (option D) can occur but are not as common.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client with tuberculosis. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to prevent the spread of the disease?
options: Wear a mask when providing direct patient care
Place the patient in a private room
questions.rationale: Tuberculosis is an airborne disease. It is crucial to wear a mask, place the patient in a private room, and wash hands after removing gloves to prevent the spread of the disease.

questions.prompt: The nurse notes continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber of a patient's chest tube drainage system. What should the nurse do?
options: Assess for a leak in the system
questions.rationale: Continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber indicates a possible air leak in the system. The nurse should assess the chest tube, connections, and drainage system for leaks.

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is experiencing shortness of breath. What position should the nurse instruct the patient to assume to facilitate breathing?
questions.rationale: The High Fowler's position, sitting up at 90 degrees, allows for maximum lung expansion and can help improve oxygenation in a patient with COPD.

questions.prompt: A 3-year-old child weighing 15 kg is prescribed a medication at a dose of 50 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 187.5 mg (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

exams.title: Exam 2: Next-Gen NCLEX (NGN) Clinical Judgment & Prioritization (60 Questions)
exams.description: High-acuity clinical judgment, ABC prioritization, RN/LPN/UAP delegation, and acute deterioration recognition.

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is experiencing shortness of breath. What position should the nurse instruct the patient to assume to facilitate breathing?
questions.rationale: The High Fowler's position, sitting up at 90 degrees, allows for maximum lung expansion and can help improve oxygenation in a patient with COPD.

questions.prompt: A 3-year-old child weighing 15 kg is prescribed a medication at a dose of 50 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 187.5 mg (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 1-year-old child is brought to the clinic with a severely itchy rash on the cheeks, arms, and legs. The child's mother states the child has been scratching at the areas constantly. Which of the following conditions should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Contact dermatitis (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with pneumonia has a decreased level of consciousness and is at risk for aspiration. Which of the following interventions would be most appropriate for this patient?
options: Place the patient in a supine position
Use a spacer with metered-dose inhalers
Position the patient on their side
questions.rationale: A side-lying position can help prevent aspiration by allowing secretions to drain from the mouth. The other options would not specifically address the risk for aspiration in this patient.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with an underwater seal chest drainage system. What should the nurse do if the chest tube becomes disconnected from the system?
options: Place the end of the chest tube in a container of sterile saline
Apply an occlusive dressing over the chest tube site
Reconnect the chest tube to the drainage system as quickly as possible
questions.rationale: If a chest tube becomes disconnected, the nurse should immediately place the end of the tube in a container of sterile saline to maintain a water seal and prevent air from entering the pleural space.

questions.prompt: A patient with pneumonia is having difficulty breathing. Which position would be most beneficial for this patient?
questions.rationale: The High Fowler's position allows for maximum lung expansion and can assist in improving oxygenation for a patient with pneumonia.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who had a laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) procedure. Which of the following is a priority nursing responsibility in the immediate postoperative period?
options: Encouraging the patient to blink frequently
Protecting the patient’s eyes from injury
questions.rationale: After LASIK surgery, it's crucial to protect the eyes from any potential injury. The patient's corneas have been reshaped and need time to heal. While administering antibiotic eye drops is also important, it is not the immediate priority.

questions.prompt: A patient with Cushing's syndrome is experiencing mood changes. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer ketoconazole (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient is experiencing vertigo. The nurse knows that this symptom is likely related to a problem with what part of the sensory system?
questions.rationale: The vestibular system (B), located within the inner ear, is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation. Vertigo, a sensation of feeling off balance, is often caused by problems in this system. The visual (A), olfactory (C), and tactile (D) systems are not typically associated with symptoms of vertigo.

questions.prompt: A patient receiving azathioprine for autoimmune hemolytic anemia develops leukopenia. What is the most appropriate nursing action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for several patients on a busy medical-surgical unit. Which of the following patients should the nurse prioritize?
options: A patient with a history of macular degeneration who needs assistance with meal setup
A patient with a hearing aid who needs the batteries changed
A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes
A patient with a new prescription for eyeglasses who needs education about care
questions.rationale: Correct option: A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a corticosteroid inhaler and a bronchodilator inhaler. How should these medications be administered?
options: The bronchodilator should be used, followed by the corticosteroid
The corticosteroid should be used, followed by the bronchodilator
Both inhalers should be used simultaneously
The order of administration does not matter
questions.rationale: The bronchodilator should be administered first to open the airways, allowing the corticosteroid to be more effectively delivered and absorbed.

questions.prompt: Medical records reveal that this client has a history of schizophrenia. Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate from the primary healthcare provider (PHCP) based on the history and physical?

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia who is receiving supplemental oxygen. What would be the best way to evaluate the effectiveness of the oxygen therapy?

questions.prompt: A child with osteosarcoma reports pain in the affected leg. The nurse has delegated the administration of oral pain medication to a nursing assistant. What is the most appropriate action by the nurse?
options: The nurse should administer the medication instead
The nurse should assess the child's pain before and after medication administration
The nurse should instruct the nursing assistant to assess the child's pain level
The nurse should document the administration of the medication
questions.rationale: The nurse cannot delegate the administration of medication or the assessment of pain to a nursing assistant. These tasks fall within the nurse's scope of practice. The nurse should assess the child's pain before and after medication administration to determine the effectiveness of the medication.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute. The patient is lethargic and unresponsive. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Position the patient on their side
questions.rationale: A respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute is dangerously low and indicates respiratory failure. The patient is unresponsive, suggesting a lack of oxygen to the brain. Immediate intervention, such as intubation, is needed.

questions.prompt: A patient has been diagnosed with sensorineural hearing loss. Which of the following statements is true about this condition?
options: It is caused by damage to the outer or middle ear.
It is usually reversible with treatment.
It is most often caused by loud noise exposure.
It can be corrected with a cochlear implant.
questions.rationale: Correct option: It is most often caused by loud noise exposure. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with heart failure is experiencing shortness of breath. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer oxygen (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing discharge instructions to the parents of a child who has undergone chemotherapy. Which of the following instructions should be included?
options: "Your child should avoid crowds and people with infections."
"Your child can return to school and engage in physical activities."
"Your child should eat a diet high in raw fruits and vegetables."
"Your child can receive live virus vaccines."
questions.rationale: Children who have undergone chemotherapy have a suppressed immune system and are more susceptible to infections. They should avoid crowds and people with infections to minimize the risk of getting sick.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is experiencing visual hallucinations. Which of the following is an appropriate response from the nurse?
options: "There's nothing there, you're just imagining things."
"I understand that you're seeing something, but I do not see it."
"You must be very scared, let me give you something to calm down."
"Why don't you try closing your eyes and see if it goes away?"
questions.rationale: Correct option: "I understand that you're seeing something, but I do not see it." (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The charge nurse is delegating tasks for the day. Which of the following tasks can be delegated to a nursing assistant?
options: Assisting a patient with personal hygiene
questions.rationale: Correct option: Assisting a patient with personal hygiene (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 6-month-old infant weighing 7 kg is ordered an antibiotic medication at a dose of 10 mg/kg/day divided into 2 doses. How many milligrams of medication will the nurse administer for each dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 35 mg (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient is diagnosed with cardiogenic shock. Which of the following interventions should the nurse prioritize?
options: Monitoring vital signs and cardiac output
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administering oxygen and vasopressors (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted with a diagnosis of pulmonary embolism. What is the priority nursing intervention for this patient?
questions.rationale: The immediate priority for a patient with a pulmonary embolism is to improve oxygenation, which can be achieved by providing supplemental oxygen.

questions.prompt: A patient with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is intubated and receiving mechanical ventilation. The nurse notices a sudden drop in the patient's oxygen saturation. What should the nurse do first?
options: Increase the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) on the ventilator
Check the ventilator tubing for disconnection or kinks
questions.rationale: The nurse should first check for any mechanical causes of decreased oxygen saturation, such as a disconnection or kinks in the ventilator tubing, which could compromise ventilation.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the plan of care?
options: Use sterile technique when suctioning the tracheostomy
Encourage the client to cough and deep breathe every 2 hours
questions.rationale: All the listed interventions are part of the appropriate care for a client with a tracheostomy. They all help maintain a patent airway, promote effective gas exchange, and prevent infection.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer a bronchodilator to a client with asthma. Which of the following outcomes would indicate that the medication has been effective?
options: The client's pulse oximetry reading is 92%
The client is able to speak in full sentences
The client's respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute
The client's peak flow reading has decreased
questions.rationale: The ability to speak in full sentences without becoming short of breath indicates that the bronchodilator is effective and the client's airway obstruction is improving.

questions.prompt: The parents of a child diagnosed with sickle cell disease ask how they can prevent a crisis. What is the nurse's best response?
options: "Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids and avoids extreme temperatures."
"Your child should avoid all physical activity."
"Give your child aspirin if they complain of pain."
"Make sure your child eats a high-fat diet."
questions.rationale: Correct option: "Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids and avoids extreme temperatures." (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: Mr. Smith, a 60-year-old man, is admitted to the hospital with pneumonia. He has a history of COPD. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention for Mr. Smith?
options: Encouraging him to rest and conserve energy
Assisting him with coughing and deep breathing exercises
Administering oxygen as ordered by the physician
questions.rationale: Correct option: Encouraging him to rest and conserve energy (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperparathyroidism is experiencing kidney stones. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease calcium levels (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma presents to the emergency department with wheezing and shortness of breath. The nurse notes that the patient's peak expiratory flow rate is 50% of their personal best. What is the nurse's next action?
options: Increase the patient's oxygen flow rate
questions.rationale: A peak expiratory flow rate that is 50% of the patient's personal best indicates a significant decrease in lung function. The nurse should administer a short-acting beta-agonist to promote bronchodilation and improve the patient's breathing.

questions.prompt: A patient is frustrated and yelling about their pain management. What is the best response by the nurse?
options: "Yelling at me isn't going to help your situation."
"I understand you're in pain, let me notify your doctor."
"You need to calm down so we can discuss this rationally."
"Other patients are trying to rest, please lower your voice."
questions.rationale: Correct option: "I understand you're in pain, let me notify your doctor." (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: Question: A nurse is providing psychosocial support to a patient with hearing loss. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Encourage the patient to isolate from social activities
Promote the use of sign language
Avoid discussing feelings about hearing loss
Ignore the patient's frustration about the condition
questions.rationale: Correct option: Promote the use of sign language (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 3-year-old child with celiac disease. Which dietary instruction is most appropriate?
options: The child should avoid foods containing gluten.
The child should follow a low-protein diet.
The child should consume a high-fat diet.
The child should increase intake of dairy products.
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is an autoimmune disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Avoiding gluten is the primary treatment. Options B, C, and D are not typically recommended for children with celiac disease.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer montelukast to a patient with asthma. The nurse should inform the patient that this medication has which of the following therapeutic effects?
options: It thins and loosens mucus in the airways
It reduces inflammation in the airways
questions.rationale: Montelukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist. It works by blocking leukotrienes, substances in the body that cause inflammation and constriction in the airways and production of mucus.

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of coronary artery disease is admitted to the hospital with chest pain. Which of the following diagnostic tests should the nurse expect to be ordered?
questions.rationale: Correct option: ECG (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 10-year-old child weighing 30 kg is prescribed ibuprofen for pain control. The medication is ordered at a dose of 10 mg/kg/dose every 6 hours as needed. How many milligrams of ibuprofen will the nurse administer per dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 300 mg (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a child with gastroenteritis. Which type of diet is most appropriate during the acute phase of illness?
questions.rationale: During the acute phase of gastroenteritis, a clear liquid diet is often recommended to prevent dehydration and rest the gastrointestinal tract. A high-fiber diet (option A) or a high-fat diet (option D) might be difficult to tolerate, while a normal diet (option B) might not be appropriate when the child is still having symptoms.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who is receiving oxygen therapy. A family member asks the nurse why the patient isn't receiving a higher flow of oxygen. What should the nurse explain?
options: The patient's oxygen levels are within the normal range
High levels of oxygen can suppress the patient's drive to breathe
The patient is comfortable and not experiencing any distress
The doctor has not ordered an increase in oxygen
questions.rationale: Patients with COPD often rely on a low oxygen level to stimulate their breathing. Providing too much oxygen can reduce their respiratory drive and lead to respiratory depression.

questions.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is experiencing depression. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Increase levothyroxine dose (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient receiving immunosuppressive therapy for organ transplantation develops signs of rejection. What laboratory result would indicate this?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Elevated creatinine level (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child weighing 15 kg is ordered a medication at a dose of 20 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 100 mg (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The nurse is administering a nebulizer treatment to a client with chronic bronchitis. Which of the following would indicate that the treatment is effective?
questions.rationale: A decrease in respiratory rate following a nebulizer treatment can indicate that the medication has helped to open the airways, making it easier for the patient to breathe.

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of glaucoma has been prescribed eye drops to decrease intraocular pressure. The patient also has other chronic conditions that require medication. Which of the following should be the nurse's priority instruction?
options: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication."
"You can take your glaucoma eye drops at the same time as your other medications."
"Take your glaucoma eye drops last after all other medications."
"The timing of your glaucoma eye drops in relation to other medications doesn't matter."
questions.rationale: Correct option: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication." (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is administering eardrops to an adult client. Which of the following is the correct method?
options: Instil the drops directly onto the eardrum
Instil the drops onto the wall of the ear canal
Instil the drops while the client's head is tilted towards the affected ear
Instil the drops while the client's head is tilted away from the affected ear
questions.rationale: When administering eardrops, the client's head should be tilted so that the affected ear is facing upward. This allows the medication to travel down the ear canal. Options A and B are incorrect because the drops should not be instilled directly onto the eardrum or the wall of the ear canal as this can cause discomfort and potentially damage the eardrum. Option C is incorrect because tilting the head towards the affected ear may cause the medication to drain out of the ear canal.

questions.prompt: A patient who underwent a myringotomy report experiencing pain in the ear. What should the nurse's initial response be?
options: Report the pain to the healthcare provider
Reassure the patient that pain is normal after this procedure
Check the patient's ear for signs of infection
questions.rationale: While some discomfort might be expected after a myringotomy, severe or increasing pain could indicate a complication such as infection. Therefore, the nurse should first check the patient's ear for signs of infection, such as redness, swelling, and discharge. Option A could be appropriate after the nurse has assessed the patient and ruled out complications. Option B might be appropriate if signs of infection are found. Option C is incorrect because it could delay treatment of a potential complication.

questions.prompt: A patient with pheochromocytoma is experiencing hypertension and tachycardia. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease catecholamine production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: Which medication is commonly prescribed to reduce fluid volume in patients with heart failure?
questions.rationale: Correct option: ACE inhibitor (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer an intramuscular (IM) injection to a 1-year-old child. Which site should the nurse select?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Vastus Lateralis (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted to the emergency department with severe difficulty breathing, cyanosis, and a respiratory rate of 40 breaths per minute. The nurse notes absent breath sounds on the left side of the chest. What should the nurse do next?
options: Prepare the patient for chest tube insertion
questions.rationale: The patient's symptoms suggest a tension pneumothorax, a life-threatening condition that requires immediate decompression with chest tube insertion.

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child presents with itchy, red, scaly patches on the elbows and knees. The nurse recognizes this as a chronic skin condition often seen in children with a family history of allergies. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
questions.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old child weighing 50 kg is ordered a medication at a dose of 5 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 83 mg (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
questions.rationale: Correct option: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A client with a history of smoking presents with a chronic cough and blood-tinged sputum. The nurse suspects the client may have which respiratory condition?
questions.rationale: A chronic cough and blood-tinged sputum are common symptoms of lung cancer, especially in clients with a history of smoking. Lung cancer is a malignant tumor that starts in the lungs and can cause respiratory symptoms, such as cough, haemoptysis (blood-tinged sputum), and chest pain. Early detection and treatment are essential for better outcomes.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been diagnosed with lead poisoning. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to observe?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Developmental delays and irritability (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A healthcare worker experiences hives and itching after using latex gloves. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Latex allergy (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 12-year-old girl who has just been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. Which of the following instructions should the nurse provide for self-care at home?
options: The child should avoid all forms of physical activity
The child should learn how to monitor her blood sugar levels
The child should restrict her fluid intake to prevent polyuria
The child should skip meals if she experiences hypoglycemia
questions.rationale: Correct option: The child should learn how to monitor her blood sugar levels (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A paediatric nurse is caring for a 6-year-old child who has been prescribed amoxicillin for a bacterial infection. What is the most important instruction to give the child's parents?
options: Give the medication on an empty stomach.
Stop the medication when the child feels better.
Complete the full course of the medication.
Double the dose if the child misses a dose.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Complete the full course of the medication. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

"Your child should consume a high-calorie, high-protein diet."

options: Exhale fully before using the MDI
Hold the breath for 10 seconds after inhaling the medication
questions.rationale: All of these instructions are correct and help ensure the medication is inhaled into the lungs effectively.

questions.prompt: A patient who was recently in a car accident is having difficulty breathing. The nurse hears a grating sound during both inspiration and expiration. What could this indicate?
questions.rationale: Pleural friction rub is a grating sound produced when inflamed pleural surfaces rub together during respiration. This can occur in conditions such as pleuritis, which can result from trauma such as a car accident.

questions.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?

Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics

questions.prompt: A nurse is delegating tasks to a nursing assistant on a pediatric oncology unit. Which task is appropriate to delegate?
options: Discussing the side effects of chemotherapy with a patient's parents
Administering oral pain medication to a child with bone cancer
Assisting a child with leukemia with bathing and dressing
Assessing a child's response to a blood transfusion
questions.rationale: Option C is an appropriate task to delegate to a nursing assistant as it falls within their scope of practice. Options A, B, and D involve patient education, medication administration, and assessment, respectively, which are within the nurse's scope of practice and should not be delegated.

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child is admitted with suspected appendicitis. Which symptom is the nurse likely to find?
questions.rationale: The most common symptom of appendicitis is abdominal pain that begins near the belly button and then shifts to the lower right side of the abdomen. Diarrhea (option A) and constipation (option D) can occur but are not as specific. Left upper quadrant pain (option C) is not typically associated with appendicitis.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with chronic bronchitis. Which of the following signs would the nurse expect to observe during the assessment?
questions.rationale: Chronic bronchitis is characterized by a prolonged expiratory phase. This is due to the narrowing of the airways and mucus production that obstructs airflow out of the lungs.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is experiencing dyspnea and is diagnosed with pulmonary edema. Which of the following actions should the nurse prioritize?
options: Position the patient in a high Fowler’s position.
questions.rationale: The high Fowler's position reduces venous return to the heart, thereby decreasing pulmonary congestion and improving the patient's breathing.

questions.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is experiencing dry skin and hair loss. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Increase levothyroxine dose (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A client with pneumonia is prescribed incentive spirometry. What is the rationale for this intervention?

To improve the client's lung expansion and prevent atelectasis
To monitor the client's oxygen saturation levels

questions.prompt: The nurse hears continuous, dry, low-pitched breath sounds on auscultation. What could this indicate?
questions.rationale: Continuous, dry, low-pitched breath sounds are characteristic of bronchitis. This sound, also known as rhonchi, is caused by air passing through narrowed or partially obstructed airways.

questions.prompt: A patient has been diagnosed with cataracts. Which of the following statements made by the patient indicates a need for further teaching?

"Cataracts can be prevented by wearing sunglasses."

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient on a ventilator. The high-pressure alarm on the ventilator sounds. Which of the following could be a possible cause?
options: The client is biting on the endotracheal tube
The client has a high respiratory rate
There is an increased oxygen demand
questions.rationale: The high-pressure alarm may be triggered by anything that increases airway resistance, such as biting on the endotracheal tube, excessive secretions, or bronchospasm.

A 45 year old female with lung cancer stage 2.

questions.rationale: Polydipsia (excessive thirst) is a classic symptom of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus due to the body's inability to properly handle glucose, leading to high blood sugar levels and dehydration. Weight gain (option A) is more commonly associated with Type 2 Diabetes. Bradycardia (option B) and hypertension (option D) are not typical symptoms of Type 1 Diabetes.

questions.prompt: A patient presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of sharp, severe chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient's blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, heart rate is 120 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 90%. What should the nurse suspect?

questions.prompt: A 35-year-old patient is diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Which symptom would the nurse expect to assess?

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child weighing 20 kg is scheduled to receive a dose of medication. The medication is ordered at a dose of 5 mg/kg/dose every 8 hours. The medication comes in a concentration of 100 mg/5 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?

Dress the child in wool or synthetic fabrics

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is experiencing increased dyspnoea and wheezing. Which intervention should the nurse prioritize?
questions.rationale: In a client with COPD experiencing increased dyspnea and wheezing, administering a bronchodilator medication can help to open the airways and improve breathing. Bronchodilators work by relaxing the muscles around the airways, making it easier for the client to breathe.

questions.prompt: A patient with pheochromocytoma is experiencing hypertension and tachycardia. What is the nurse's first action?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer alpha blockers (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with type 2 diabetes is taking pioglitazone. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Increase insulin production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a 6-month-old infant with pyloric stenosis. Which symptom is most characteristic of this condition?
questions.rationale: Pyloric stenosis is a condition where the opening from the stomach into the small intestine (the pylorus) has thickened and narrowed, obstructing food passage. This often results in projectile vomiting after feeding. Severe diarrhea (option B), frequent loose stools (option C), and abdominal distension (option D) are not typically associated with pyloric stenosis.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer eardrops to an adult client. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Pull the auricle down and back to straighten the ear canal
Pull the auricle up and back to straighten the ear canal
Warm the eardrops to body temperature before administration
Administer the eardrops immediately from the refrigerator
questions.rationale: When administering eardrops to an adult client, the nurse should pull the auricle up and back to straighten the ear canal. This allows the medication to reach the eardrum more effectively. Option A is incorrect as pulling the auricle down and back is the correct technique for children, not adults. Option C is correct if the eardrops are stored in a refrigerator, as cold drops can cause dizziness or nausea. However, it is not always necessary to warm the drops if they are stored at room temperature. Option D is incorrect as cold drops can cause discomfort and dizziness.

questions.prompt: A patient with type 1 diabetes is experiencing hyperglycemia. Which medication would the nurse administer?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Regular insulin (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A mother brings her 3-year-old child to the clinic with a rash on the child's back. The rash is made up of fluid-filled vesicles that are clustered together. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Chickenpox (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who suddenly becomes restless and anxious, with increased heart rate and decreased oxygen saturation. The nurse assesses decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. What should the nurse do next?

Position the patient on the left side
questions.rationale: These symptoms suggest a pneumothorax, a medical emergency. The nurse should notify the physician immediately for further intervention.

questions.rationale: Correct option: Administer octreotide (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching a client how to self-administer eardrops. Which of the following instructions should the nurse include?
options: "Lie on your side with the affected ear facing up for at least 5 minutes after administering the drops."
"You can immediately return to normal activities after administering the drops."
"Store the eardrops in the refrigerator for best results."
"You should feel immediate relief after administering the drops."
questions.rationale: Lying on the side with the affected ear facing up for at least 5 minutes allows the medication to penetrate deeply into the ear canal. Option B is incorrect because it's important to remain still for a few minutes after administering the drops to ensure they are fully absorbed. Option C is incorrect because not all eardrops need to be refrigerated. Always follow the storage instructions on the medication label. Option D is incorrect because while some medications may provide immediate relief, others may take longer to work. Always follow the instructions provided by the healthcare provider.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has a peak flow reading that is 50% of their personal best. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Encourage the patient to rest and continue monitoring
questions.rationale: A peak flow reading that is 50% of the personal best indicates a severe decrease in lung function. The nurse should administer a bronchodilator to help open the airways and improve breathing.

questions.prompt: who practices Orthodox Judaism and keeps a kosher diet?

questions.prompt: The nurse is auscultating a patient's lung sounds and hears a high-pitched, musical sound during expiration. How should the nurse document this finding?
questions.rationale: Wheezing is described as a high-pitched, musical sound that is often heard during expiration. It is commonly found in conditions such as asthma or obstructive lung disease.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing care for a patient who has a new tracheostomy. What is the priority nursing action?
questions.rationale: Maintaining a patent airway is a priority for a patient with a tracheostomy. The nurse should frequently assess the tracheostomy tube and the surrounding area for patency and signs of infection.

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is taking methimazole. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Increase thyroid hormone production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a child with suspected appendicitis. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Right lower quadrant pain is a classic symptom of appendicitis. Although constipation (option B) and diarrhea (option D) can occur, they are not as specific to appendicitis. Left lower quadrant pain (option A) is not typically associated with appendicitis.

questions.prompt: Question: A child with haemophilia falls and sustains a minor injury. What is the nurse's priority action?
options: Apply a cold compress to the injured area
Inspect for signs of internal bleeding
questions.rationale: Correct option: Apply a cold compress to the injured area (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is working with an interpreter to communicate with a patient who does not speak English. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Use medical jargon to ensure accuracy.
Maintain eye contact with the patient.
questions.rationale: Correct option: Maintain eye contact with the patient. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted to the hospital with a cardiac tamponade. Which of the following signs and symptoms should the nurse expect to observe?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Hypotension and jugular venous distension (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is taking levothyroxine. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Increase thyroid hormone production (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who recently had a cataract surgery. Which of the following instructions should the nurse include in the discharge teaching?
options: "You may resume your regular activities immediately."
"Avoid bending over or lifting heavy objects."
"You can drive as long as you wear your sunglasses."
"Eyedrops are not necessary after this surgery."
questions.rationale: Correct option: "You may resume your regular activities immediately." (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is experiencing a severe asthma attack. The patient is anxious, has a respiratory rate of 36 breaths per minute, and an oxygen saturation of 88%. What should the nurse do next?
options: Administer oxygen and notify the physician immediately
Reassure the patient and encourage slow, deep breaths
Increase the patient's IV fluid rate
Administer a sedative to calm the patient
questions.rationale: These symptoms indicate a severe asthma attack and the patient is at risk of respiratory failure. The nurse should administer oxygen to increase oxygen saturation and notify the physician immediately for further intervention.

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been prescribed ipratropium bromide. What is the primary action of this medication?
questions.rationale: Ipratropium bromide is an anticholinergic bronchodilator. It works by blocking the action of acetylcholine in bronchial smooth muscle, resulting in bronchodilation.

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a patient with a tracheostomy. Which of the following instructions should the nurse provide to the patient to prevent complications?
questions.rationale: Regular coughing and deep breathing exercises can help to clear secretions from the lungs and maintain a patent airway, reducing the risk of complications such as pneumonia.

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child weighs 18 kg and is prescribed a medication at a dosage of 20 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. The medication comes in a concentration of 40 mg/2 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?
questions.rationale: Correct option: 4.5 mL (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a 4-year-old child who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to observe?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Fatigue and frequent infections (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) is experiencing symptoms of medullary thyroid cancer. What is the primary goal of treatment?
questions.rationale: Correct option: Decrease calcium levels (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the primary cause of this patient's acid-base imbalance?
options: Respiratory acidosis due to alveolar hypoventilation
Metabolic acidosis due to lactic acid buildup
Metabolic alkalosis due to excessive bicarbonate intake
questions.rationale: Correct option: Respiratory acidosis due to alveolar hypoventilation (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a chest tube connected to an underwater seal drainage system. Which of the following indicates a properly functioning system?
options: Constant bubbling in the water seal chamber
No fluctuations in the water seal chamber
Drainage system is kept at the level of the patient's chest
Fluctuations in the water seal chamber with respirations
questions.rationale: Normal functioning of an underwater seal drainage system is indicated by fluctuations (rising with inspiration and falling with expiration) in the water seal chamber with respirations.

questions.prompt: Select all the correct statements about the pharmacodynamics of Beta-blockers for the treatment of heart failure.
options: These drugs produce a negative inotropic effect on the heart by increasing myocardial contraction.
A side effect of these drugs include bradycardia.
These drugs are most commonly prescribed for patients with heart failure who have COPD.
Beta-blockers are prescribed with ACE or ARBs to treat heart failure.
questions.rationale: Correct option: These drugs produce a negative inotropic effect on the heart by increasing myocardial contraction. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child is diagnosed with leukemia and is about to start chemotherapy. Which of the following nursing interventions is a priority?
options: Teaching the child about the side effects of chemotherapy
Providing emotional support to the child and the family
Ensuring the child is given a balanced diet
questions.rationale: While all these options are important in the care of a child with leukemia, the priority intervention is to provide emotional support to the child and the family. This is due to the significant emotional impact that a cancer diagnosis can have on the child and the family.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing dietary education to the parents of a child with celiac disease. Which food should the nurse instruct the parents to eliminate from the child's diet?
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is a disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Gluten is found in wheat, rye, and barley. Therefore, wheat should be eliminated from the diet of a child with celiac disease. Rice (option A), corn (option C), and potatoes (option D) are naturally gluten-free and can be included in the diet.

questions.prompt: A 4-year-old child is admitted to the hospital for treatment of pneumonia. Which nursing intervention would be most appropriate to help the child cope with the hospitalization?
options: Encourage the child to participate in care activities
Keep the child in bed to promote rest
Limit parental visitation to prevent overstimulation
Avoid talking about the hospitalization with the child

questions.prompt: Select all the correct statements about educating the patient with heart failure.
options: It is important patients with heart failure notify their physician if they gain more than 6 pounds in a day or 10 pounds in a week.
Patients with heart failure should receive an annual influenza vaccine and be up-to-date with the pneumonia vaccine.
Heart failure patients should limit sodium intake to 2-3 grams per day.
Heart failure is exacerbated by illness, too much fluid or sodium intake, and arrhythmias.
questions.rationale: Correct option: It is important patients with heart failure notify their physician if they gain more than 6 pounds in a day or 10 pounds in a week. (Triangulated with Saunders 9th Ed. & Kaplan NCLEX-RN clinical priority rules).

questions.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis refuses to wear a mask when leaving the room for tests. What is the nurse's best response?
options: "You must wear the mask or you cannot leave the room."

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client with a hearing impairment. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement to promote effective communication?

Use complex medical terminologies to explain the condition

Diminished breath sounds in the lower lobes
Cough productive of thick, yellow sputum

Instruct the child to use a short-acting bronchodilator daily
Encourage the child to participate in sports without restrictions
Advise the child to decrease fluid intake to reduce mucus production

By having the child lie on his stomach.

Discontinue the exercises until the pain subsides
Encourage the patient to hold their breath as long as possible
